newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down on profit-taking.

text.p: Thai stocks closed slightly lower in thin trade on Wednesday as investors sold stocks, mainly large capitalised banking issues, and took profits while they awaited first quarter earnings, brokers said.

"The index fell because of profit-taking. Moody's decision earlier today on downgrading Thailand's long-term foreign currency debt rating didn't have an impact on the market as most investors already discounted the news," said Payuha Boonsiri of Nithipat Capital.
The composite SET index fell 2.73 points to 712.63 on 2.7 billion baht turnover.
The SET-50 index slipped 0.28 point to 53.46.
Moody's Investors Service also said it was cutting the long-term senior debt and deposit ratings of five Thai banks to A3.

"Investors think the first quarter earnings for finance firms due to be released by April 21 won't be impressive and that was why they decided to sell today. Also, they wanted to hold cash for an upcoming long weekend holidays," Payuha said.
The market will be closed on April 14-15 to mark the traditional Thai New year.
The listed banks downgraded by Moody's were Bangkok Bank, which declined three baht to 187. It was first-ranked on the active list.
Others were Thai Farmers Bank slipping one to 122, Siam Commercial Bank unchanged at 137 and Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand dipping 0.50 to 69.50.
Large capitalised TelecomAsia gained 0.50 to 47 and Siam Cement rose 12 to 640.
